tools.name: ping
tools.description: Check the key works and show its plan limits. Read-only; creates nothing.

tools.name: create-watch
tools.description: Start watching a URL; checks it on a schedule and records changes. Does one check now to set the baseline; does not notify for the baseline. Give at most one of keyword or condition+threshold, and one of selector or json_path.

tools.name: list-watches
tools.description: List your watches, newest first, 10 per page. Read-only.

tools.name: get-watch
tools.description: Show one watch with its last value, status and webhook secret. Read-only.

tools.name: delete-watch
tools.description: Stop and remove a watch. Its recorded changes stay readable. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list-changes
tools.description: List recorded changes. With no cursor returns the 10 newest; with since returns changes after that cursor, oldest first, for polling. Read-only.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get-watch" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Show one watch with its last value, status and webhook secret. Read-only.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create-watch · Private data: create-watch, get-watch · Public sink: create-watch, get-watch · Destructive: delete-watch.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create-watch · Private data: create-watch, get-watch · Public sink: create-watch, get-watch · Destructive: delete-watch

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
